description: We are a team interested in space exploration, NASA mission, web development, research, and data visualization. Our project explores the stories of NASA spacecraft and equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars, turning space history and scientific data into an interactive experience. We are looking for team members interested in coding, design, research, storytelling, data analysis, and space science who are enthusiastic about collaborating and building an engaging NASA Space Apps project.
summary:
NASA Ghosts Explorer is an interactive web-based space exploration project that tells the stories of NASA spacecraft, landers, rovers, and other equipment that were left behind on the Moon and Mars after their missions. The project transforms mission and historical data into an engaging digital experience, allowing users to explore these “space ghosts,” understand where they are, what they were designed to do, and why they remain scientifically and historically important.

The project combines NASA-related datasets and interactive web technologies to create an educational space museum experience. It aims to help students and space enthusiasts discover the forgotten stories behind humanity’s early exploration of the Moon and Mars.
details:
NASA Ghosts Explorer is an interactive web-based project that brings attention to NASA spacecraft, landers, rovers, and other exploration equipment that were left behind after their missions on the Moon and Mars. The project presents their stories in an engaging and easy-to-understand digital experience, helping users discover what each mission was designed to do, where the equipment was used, and why these abandoned or inactive explorers remain historically and scientifically important.

The website is designed as an interactive space museum that makes space exploration information more accessible to students and space enthusiasts. Instead of presenting mission information only as technical data, the project focuses on storytelling and exploration, encouraging users to learn about the history and legacy of planetary exploration.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python, with NASA-related data and resources integrated into the website. The project is designed to work as a web application and can be accessed through a browser. The team also considered usability, simplicity, educational value, visual presentation, and the reliability of the information used.

The creative aspect of the project is the idea of presenting forgotten or inactive space equipment as “ghosts” of exploration. This storytelling approach turns historical mission data into an interactive experience and gives users a different perspective on the lasting impact of space exploration.

The intended impact is to increase interest in planetary science and NASA missions, especially among students and young space enthusiasts. By showing that even equipment that is no longer active can have an important story, the project encourages users to appreciate the achievements, challenges, and legacy of space exploration.
